note: The prompt templates a kind profile names, one per built-in kind plus `generic`, `anchor` and `video`. A template is what makes `gen image` one command rather than one per kind - see specs/gen-fal/design.md. `{prompt}` is what the caller asked for and is substituted verbatim; `{width}` and `{height}` are the kind's cell, which is the *logical* sprite cell and not the size the image is generated at. `{style}` is how the art is drawn, and it comes from `--style` or from the kind - see src/ssc/data/styles.json and specs/generation-style/. A template states what is true of the output whatever it looks like and never how it is drawn: a template that says `no anti-aliased edges` has answered a question that was somebody else's to answer, which is why `box-art` is the one template with no style slot and says its look outright. Templates ask for the flat chroma green core/bgremove.py keys by default, because generating on a background `tool bgremove` cannot remove is how a paid image becomes unusable - `box-art` is the other exception there, and it is deliberate: box art keeps its setting because it is never cut out. Magenta is the other preset and is the better key for a character carrying a lot of green, but it has to be asked for on both sides: the prompt and `bgremove --chroma magenta`. A template may also name any of `gen.VARIABLES` as `{name}`, `{prop}` and so on; every one it names must be supplied with `--var`, and a call missing one is refused rather than sent, because the literal text `{name}` in a paid prompt is the failure this exists to stop. `video` and `walk` overlap heavily on purpose: `video` is the base every in-place animation needs and `walk` is that base plus the motion of a walk cycle, and folding the two into one would tell an idle animation to alternate its legs. Neither states a look: a clip animates an image that already has one.

templates.box-art:
{prompt}

Character box art for a roster or character-select screen: {name}, a {archetype}, at {width}x{height}, portrait. Wearing {costume}, carrying {prop}, set in {setting}. Three-quarter hero composition, full body or near full body, filling most of the height. Painterly rendered illustration - not flat cel shading, not pixel art. The silhouette still reads as one clear shape, because this character exists as sprites elsewhere and the two have to look like the same person. The setting is this character's own - the place the description above puts them - and borrows no motif, palette or landmark from anywhere else in the roster. It sits behind and around them, supporting them, never crossing in front of them and never competing for the eye. No text, no logo, no UI, no watermark, no border, no frame, and no runes, glyphs or written symbols unless the description above asks for them.
templates.video:
{prompt}

Animate this single subject in place. Preserve the identity exactly as the input image has it - the same look, proportions, palette, costume and silhouette - and hold the orientation the input image already has for the entire clip. It does not turn, pivot, rotate or show a quarter-turn view at any point, and does not translate across the frame. The camera is fixed and centred, the framing does not change, and the motion loops back to the first frame. The background stays the same flat neutral field it already is: it does not become a floor, a room, a horizon, an outdoor scene, a perspective grid or a shadow plane. One character, no scene, no added props, no labels, no arrows, no cuts, no zoom, no text, no watermark. No attack, no weapon swing, no magic, fireball, spell effect, smoke, particle, glow, trail or impact.
templates.walk:
{prompt}

Animate this single character into a simple in-place walk cycle, facing {direction} for the entire clip. Preserve the identity exactly as the input image has it - the same look, proportions, palette, costume and silhouette. The character does not turn, pivot, rotate or show a quarter-turn view at any point, and does not translate across the frame. Readable game-sprite motion: alternating leg steps, subtle vertical bobbing, minimal arm swing, light clothing and equipment sway, both feet staying visible. The camera is fixed and centred, the framing does not change, and the cycle loops back to the first frame. The background stays the same flat neutral field it already is: it does not become a floor, a room, a horizon, an outdoor scene, a perspective grid or a shadow plane. One character, no scene, no added props, no labels, no arrows, no cuts, no zoom, no text, no watermark. No attack, no weapon swing, no magic, fireball, spell effect, smoke, particle, glow, trail or impact.
